security_and_integrity_rules: Use only the tenant-registered service and its KMS key reference; never accept a caller-selected KMS locator or private material.
Reject managed and read-only services before any provider rotation; the shared managed KMS key is not tenant-rotatable through this route.
Rotate inside KMS; never export or hold a private key.
Report provider rotation and publication failures without exposing provider credentials or raw upstream errors.
Do not claim a completed rotation in stored state when the provider did not rotate a key.

Only one rotation may hold a tenant lease through registry reload, provider rotation, and whole-registry save. Deny another in-flight rotation for that tenant before calling the provider; release by lease owner on every exit, with bounded expiry if the request is cancelled.

Fence each whole-registry save by the current lease owner. Public config, internal registry, and publication saves must use the same tenant lease; an unchanged KMS binding keeps server-owned rotation history, and a rebound key clears it.

Read the Transit key version and persist a tenant/KMS-identity reconciliation marker with that baseline before the Transit POST. A service rebind cannot clear this marker or authorize another POST against the unresolved identity.

Write pending registry state, the KMS-identity marker, and a service-level marker index in one owner-fenced Redis script. A lost reply after a completed script leaves all three discoverable; a Redis runtime write failure can leave partial state and requires governed repair. The service-level index lists unresolved operations after a rebind or removal without preventing a different new key from rotating.

Let a detached bounded task complete KMS rotation and state persistence after client cancellation. Clear the marker on confirmed success or definite pre-send/authorization failure; retain it after an ambiguous provider outcome and block another rotation.
Internal reconciliation checks the same tenant, service, KMS identity, and operation ID and finalizes only one stable version advance. An unchanged or ambiguous version does not clear the marker.

Internal whole-registry PUT remains an explicit replacement of client-owned routing and purpose bindings; it preserves server-owned rotation fields for an unchanged KMS identity. Registry appenders must acquire the tenant lease before loading the registry and save with that same lease.

Public config PATCH responds with its saved snapshot, and JWKS/DID publication holds the tenant lease from service and KMS key read through document publication and capability update. JWKS and DID document writes check the live lease owner atomically at commit, so an expired publication cannot write a stale key.
A rotated key invalidates a stale certificate; public publication must revalidate the certificate against the current KMS public key.
reviewed_divergence: The Python handler recorded last_rotated_at and appended previous_versions even when the provider returned ok=false. Rust must fail closed and avoid claiming rotation on provider failure, while retaining the released response field names for completed rotations. Rust also rejects a future activate_at because Transit rotates immediately; the Python path accepted a future annotation without scheduling activation.
